context: Here k=3. The table gives the input array and its indices. The pointer i is an input index. The min-heap's level-order array is heap. Its smallest candidate is at heap index 0, and its left and right children, if present, are at heap indices 1 and 2. An input index identifies an element's origin. A heap index gives its current position.

Push the first k inputs onto the heap in order. Then compare each remaining value with the root. If the value exceeds the root, pop the root and push the new value. Otherwise, skip it. The tables are named by step. When a comparison or skip leaves the heap unchanged, the diagram refers to the table listing those candidates and their input indices.
description: The root holds the smallest candidate. Replacing it with a larger new value preserves the k largest values among the inputs processed so far. Checking the root takes O(1) time. Adjusting the heap after a push or pop takes O(log k) time.

frames.announcement: Push 1 onto the empty heap, giving [1].
frames.explanation: At i=0, read 1 and push it onto the empty heap. There is one candidate, [1], and the root is 1.
frames.key_state: The 1 at input index i=0 has been pushed. The heap has one entry, [1], with 1 at the root.
frames.title: Push 1 onto the empty heap

frames.announcement: Push 7. No sift-up is needed, and the heap is now [1, 7].
frames.explanation: At i=1, read 7 and push it at heap index 1. Its parent, 1, is smaller than 7, so no sift-up is needed. The two candidates are [1, 7], with 1 at the root.
frames.key_state: The 7 at input index i=1 has been pushed. The heap has two entries, [1, 7], with 1 at the root.
frames.title: Push 7 onto the heap

frames.announcement: Push 6 to complete the initial three candidates, [1, 7, 6], with 1 at the root.
frames.explanation: At i=2, read 6 and push it at heap index 2. The three candidates are [1, 7, 6], with 1 at the root. The first k=3 inputs are all in the heap. Next, compare the remaining elements with the root.
frames.key_state: The 6 at input index i=2 has been pushed. The three initial entries are [1, 7, 6], with 1 at the root.

state_tables.caption: Step 3 candidates: all three initial entries

frames.title: Push 6 to complete the initial candidates

frames.announcement: Compare 3 with root 1. Since 3 > 1, prepare to replace the root. The heap has not yet changed.
frames.explanation: At i=3, the current value, 3, exceeds the smallest candidate, 1. A replacement is pending. This step only compares: nothing has been popped or pushed. The three candidates remain [1, 7, 6], with 1 at the root. For the candidates and their input indices, see “Step 3 candidates: all three initial entries.”
frames.key_state: At input index i=3, the current value 3 > root 1, so a replacement is pending. The heap still has three entries, [1, 7, 6], with 1 at the root.
frames.title: Compare the current value, 3, with root 1

frames.announcement: Pop the old root, 1. The heap temporarily holds two entries, [6, 7], while 3 waits to be pushed.
frames.explanation: With i still at 3, pop the old root, 1. The remaining heap is [6, 7], temporarily rooted at 6. It holds only k−1=2 candidates because 3 has yet to be pushed. This is an intermediate state of the replacement: no result has been missed, and the round is not yet complete.
frames.key_state: At input index i=3, the old root, 1, has been popped. The heap temporarily has k−1=2 entries, [6, 7], with 6 at the root. The current value, 3, is waiting to be pushed.

state_tables.caption: Step 5 candidates: intermediate state after popping 1

frames.title: Pop the old root, 1

frames.announcement: Push 3 and sift it up to become the new root. There are again three candidates, [3, 7, 6].
frames.explanation: With i still at 3, push 3 and sift it up to the root. There are again k=3 candidates, [3, 7, 6], and the new root is 3. These are the three largest of the first four inputs.
frames.key_state: At input index i=3, the value 3 has been pushed and sifted up. The heap again has three entries, [3, 7, 6], with 3 at the root.
frames.title: Push 3 onto the heap

frames.announcement: Compare 2 with root 3. Since 2 < 3, do not replace the root.
frames.explanation: At i=4, the current value, 2, is smaller than the root, 3, so it does not qualify for replacement. This step only compares. The three candidates remain [3, 7, 6]. For the candidates and their input indices, see “Step 6 candidates: after adding 3.”
frames.key_state: At input index i=4, the current value 2 < root 3. No replacement occurs. The heap still has three entries, [3, 7, 6], with 3 at the root.
frames.title: Compare the current value, 2, with root 3

frames.announcement: Skip 2. The three candidates remain [3, 7, 6], and all inputs have been processed.
frames.explanation: At i=4, skip 2 because it is smaller than root 3. Nothing is popped or pushed. The three candidates remain [3, 7, 6], with 3 at the root. All inputs have been processed. For the candidates and their input indices, see “Step 6 candidates: after adding 3.”
frames.key_state: The 2 at input index i=4 has been skipped, completing the input. The three entries are still [3, 7, 6], with 3 at the root.
frames.title: Skip 2

frames.announcement: Return the min-heap [3, 7, 6]. The result is not in ascending order.
frames.explanation: The traversal is over, with no current input index. Return the min-heap [3, 7, 6] directly. The table gives the input index of each candidate. The root is 3, but its left and right children, 7 and 6, need not be in ascending order. No additional sort is performed.
frames.key_state: The traversal is over, with no current input index. Return the three-entry min-heap [3, 7, 6], rooted at 3. The result is not in ascending order.

state_tables.caption: Step 9: final candidates and their origins

frames.title: Return the three candidates

result: The heap stores at most k candidates, so it uses O(k) space. The total time complexity is O(n log k).
summary: Keep at most k candidates. Compare the smallest candidate with each new element to retain the k largest values seen so far.
title: Finding the top k with a min-heap
